title: Practical First-Week Obsidian Checklist and Skill Handbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, practical first-week onboarding kit intended to live in a new hire's Obsidian vault (or similar notes app). Focus: get a cross-functional new hire in Platform/Infra or adjacent teams to useful, confident context in 10 business days.

Audience:
- New engineer joining platform, infra, SRE or platform-adjacent squads
- Buddy/mentor who will run shadow sessions and tasks
- Hiring manager as a checklist for early signals and initial feedback

High-level goals (week 0-2):
- Day0: account access and dev environment green (minimal friction)
- Day1: shadow a pairing session, read service map, run a tiny non-prod deploy
- By EOW1: add one small fix in a low-risk repo and ship a reviewable patch
- By EOW2: own a repeatable runbook step (restart + validate) and present a 10m mini-knowledge share

Owner & versioning:
- Doc owner: Priya Shah (people-ops)
- Local copy recommended in team repo: /team-onboard/obsidian-templates/first-week.md
- Status: draft — iter after two hires from Q3 pilot

Pre-boarding (before day 0) checklist for manager + people-ops (tickable in Obsidian):
- [ ] Offer accepted and start date confirmed
- [ ] HW shipped (dev laptop + dongle) with tracking number
- [ ] Primary accounts created: Google, Slack, GitHub org access, CI accounts
- [ ] VPN / corp network access request submitted to infra (link to ticket)
- [ ] Role-specific accesses requested (k8s dev namespace, staging credentials)
- [ ] Buddy assigned & intro email scheduled
- [ ] 1st week calendar: 30/60/90 intro block, daily 1:1 on calendar

Day0: arrival checklist (practical friction removal)
- [ ] Confirm laptop boot + corp login works
- [ ] Complete SSO MFA and security briefing (10m)
- [ ] Join Slack channels: #team-<team>, #eng-all, #prod-incidents, #onboarding-ops
- [ ] Confirm GitHub access, fork repo, run 'make dev' locally
- [ ] Quick wins doc opened: find a small issue tagged 'good-first-bug'
- [ ] Link important docs into Obsidian: service map, runbooks, deployment playbook

Day1: learning + low-risk pairing
- Morning: 1:1 with manager (expectations, intro to roadmap)
- Mid: buddy shadow session (pair to observe CI -> deploy pipeline)
- Afternoon: reproduce a staging dev workflow and open a sandbox PR
- End of day: fill out 'Day1 log' note: three things learned, two questions, one blocker

Day2-5: gradual ownership + micro-deep dives
- Shadow sessions (2x 45m slots):
  - Debugging trace for service X (45m)
  - Local k8s dev surfacing + sidecar debug (45m)
- Tasks: pick one small ticket with guidance, implement and ship with code review
- Buddy runbook handoff: watch, then lead the restart process once in staging
- Mini-knowledge-share prep: new hire prepares a 10m slide-free talk on a learned area

Week 2: handoff + signals for hiring manager
- New hire should:
  - Ship at least one accepted PR with tests or relevant docs
  - Run a non-prod deploy end-to-end with owner oversight
  - Present 10m knowledge share to team + collect 3 feedback items
- Manager signals to collect: ramp-confidence score (1-5), autonomy examples, blockers list

Buddy responsibilities (practical):
- Schedule 90m/week for first 2 weeks for shadow + feedback
- Curate a short reading queue (max 6 links) — service overview, CI flow, primary repo README
- Assign first PR and give an explicit acceptance criteria checklist
- Provide timely code review (<= 48h) and pair-review if large

Skill deep-dive matrix (use for EOY evaluation & early problems):
- Core infra familiarity: Docker / k8s basics — target: can reproduce a local pod + logs (signal: completed steps log)
- CI/CD literacy: understands pipeline primitives and can author one simple job
- Observability: knows primary dashboards and can interpret a spike metric
- Debugging: can run a trace, find the offending service, open an incident ticket (non-prod)
- Communication: presents a clear 10m summary with next-steps

Interview rubric (for fast rehire / backfill decisions during ramp):
- Purpose: light rubric for hiring managers to confirm earlier hiring signals match actual ramp progress. Use after week 2 interview or cross-check before extending offers for other candidates.
- Dimensions (score 1-5):
  - Technical fundamentals (data structures, systems thinking) — weight 30%
  - Code hygiene & shipping (PRs, tests, doc) — weight 25%
  - Troubleshooting & triage (logs, metrics, debugging flow) — weight 20%
  - Collaboration & communication (async updates, knowledge share) — weight 15%
  - Product sense / impact orientation — weight 10%
- Quick guidance: a hire passing week 2 should score >= 3 on fundamentals and >= 3 on troubleshooting.

Hiring plan snippet (compact, to keep near this doc):
- Role: Platform Engineer IC2
- Target lead time: 28-35 days from req open to offer
- Interview loop: take-home + 2x 45m live sessions (systems + code), 1x culture/peer match
- Offer checklist: hiring manager sign-off, compensation calibration, hiring packet to candidate with 10-day onboarding outline

Common Gotchas / Notes to self (raw):
- Obsidian is optional; main point is a single living note with links. Some hires prefer Notion — replicate the table-of-contents export.
- Watch for blocked GitHub org invites (often step that delays day1) — escalate to infra ops ticket if > 4h
- VPN access is often slower for international hires; pre-submit in week -2 when possible

Template: Day1 log (copy into new hire vault)
- Date:
- 3 things I learned:
  1.
  2.
  3.
- 2 questions I want answered:
  1.
  2.
- 1 blocker and who I asked for help:

Mini-knowledge-share template (10m):
- Topic headline (1 sentence)
- Why it matters (2 bullets)
- 3 concrete learnings / takeaways
- One suggested next step for the team

Follow-ups and iteration plan:
- Run pilot for two hires on Platform Q4 -> iterate templates
- Collect feedback in a retrospective doc (link placeholder) and add a short L2 checklist for managers

Open questions (to resolve with People Ops & Eng Leads):
- Should we formalize a 10-day acceptance survey for new hires? (ops vs team signal)
- Best person to manage hardware tracking for remote builders (people-ops vs ops procurement)
- SLA for review turnaround during week1 (target 48h accepted, escalate path)

Quick links (put these in new hire obsidian front page):
- Team service map: (confluence link)
- Primary repo: github.com/redwood/platform-core
- How to get k8s dev namespace: jira link
- Oncall runbooks: confluence-runbooks

Notes to reviewer:
- This is intentionally compact — aim for actionable over comprehensive. Copy this into team-specific variants: infra, serving-runtime, console.
- TODO: add checklist variant for interns and contractor hires (shorter access list).

-- end of doc --
